title: DreamFusion: Text-to-3D using 2D Diffusion
layout_note: Left half: a 3-D render chain (density and albedo cubes in a NeRF panel, then normals, shading and colour cubes, then a camera viewing the colour cube). Right half: the rendering is noised and passed through a frozen diffusion panel, and the noise residual returns along a long arrow at the bottom that runs back to the NeRF panel, closing the loop.
grouping: Two tinted rounded panels name the two models: a pink panel (labelled NeRF in a white tag, with the MLP name) holds the density and albedo cubes, and a cyan panel (labelled Imagen in a white tag) holds the text prompt, frozen text encoder and U-Net. The bottom return arrow is filled with a pink-to-cyan gradient, joining the two panel colours.
shapes_depth: Every 3-D quantity is a thin grey wireframe cube holding a rendered object coloured by that quantity (rainbow density, albedo, normals, grey shading, final colour). Light is a yellow sun icon with a yellow band arrow; the camera is a small dark camera glyph with grey frustum lines to a tilted image plane. Images are square photo tiles: the rendering, Gaussian noise, noised latent, denoised output and the residual. Network parts are 3-D extruded block shapes (Transformer slab, U-Net wedge) with padlock icons for frozen weights. Flow arrows are broad flat light-grey block arrows; labels are math under each picture.
proposed_highlight: The new training signal is the wide gradient-filled arrow labelled with its text, running the full width beneath the figure back into the NeRF panel; the pretrained model is marked as frozen by padlock icons, not by colour.
lesson: Draw each rendered quantity (density, albedo, normals, shading, colour) as its own wireframe cube holding the object coloured by that quantity, and close the loop with one long gradient-tinted return arrow whose two end colours match the two model panels it connects.
notes: venue ICLR from Semantic Scholar (venue_source: semantic-scholar); year = arXiv preprint year (2209.14988). The figure embeds many rendered and photo tiles; the measured palette is over the whole raster.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: training: the NeRF is optimised per prompt with a frozen diffusion prior (score distillation); no network is trained on a dataset

core.what: a loop from a pink NeRF panel on the left through rendering and noising into a cyan frozen Imagen panel on the right, closed by a long pink-to-cyan gradient arrow along the bottom labelled 'Backpropagate onto NeRF weights'

relations.form: broad grey block arrows run left to right through the render chain to Imagen, down to the predicted noise and back right-to-left to the residual, and a long gradient arrow returns along the bottom into the NeRF panel

the differentiable renderer is a chain of wireframe cubes, density -> normals (via grad tau) -> shading (n . l, lit by a sun-icon P(light)) -> colour, then a camera glyph P(camera) projects to the rendering tile
the rendering and a Gaussian-noise tile meet at a '+' to form the noised image z_t entering the Imagen panel, and the quoted text prompt drops into the frozen Transformer and U-Net from above
the predicted noise tile and the sampled noise tile sit on one row with a grey arrow giving the residual tile eps_hat - eps, the compared terms drawn as images
every 3-D quantity (density, albedo, normals, shading, colour) is the same peacock rendered inside a thin wireframe cube and coloured by that quantity

channels.colour: panel tint = model: pink = NeRF (trainable), cyan = Imagen (frozen, also padlock icons); the gradient arrow blends the two tints to show the update going from one to the other; inside the cubes colour is the rendered quantity itself
channels.shape: wireframe cube = a 3-D field, square tile = an image, extruded box = network block, sun and camera icons = sampled light and viewpoint
channels.line: broad light-grey block arrows = forward data, thin grey lines = camera rays, the gradient-filled arrow = backpropagation
channels.frame: rounded tinted panels group the NeRF parameters and the frozen Imagen model

quality.strengths: Every intermediate is drawn as the real peacock in its own representation (density, albedo, normals, shading, colour, noise, denoised image, residual), so the compared noise terms are visible between the model that makes them and the gradient they produce; the training loop is drawn as one closed path whose return arrow carries both panel colours.
quality.weaknesses: The many broad grey arrows have a uniform weight that does not separate the main path from side inputs, and the rendering-to-Imagen path makes a diagonal jump with a large gap; the residual row reads right-to-left against the rest of the figure; the shading step's curved arrow from normals with a starred multiply is hard to follow.

insights.structure: Left half a 3-D render chain (pink NeRF panel holding density and albedo cubes, then normals, shading and colour cubes, a sun and a camera); right half the rendering plus noise passed into a cyan Imagen panel with text prompt, frozen Transformer and U-Net.
insights.data: Every 3-D quantity is a thin wireframe cube holding the peacock coloured by that quantity; images (rendering, Gaussian noise, noised latent, denoised output, residual) are square photo tiles with math labels underneath.
insights.emphasis: A long bottom arrow 'Backpropagate onto NeRF weights' filled with a pink-to-cyan gradient joins the two panel colours and closes the loop back to the NeRF panel.
insights.flow: Broad light-grey block arrows run left to right through rendering, then down and back right-to-left along the bottom to the NeRF panel; light enters as a yellow band arrow from the sun.
insights.avoid: Many grey block arrows of the same weight cross the middle with no labels, and the camera frustum lines tangle with them, so the order between shading, camera and rendering is hard to trace.

arrangement.units: one loop composition with two tinted rounded sub-panels naming the two models (pink NeRF bottom-left, cyan Imagen top-right), each with a white name tag
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted text prompt in typewriter font at the top of the Imagen panel; Gaussian noise as a photo tile in the middle
arrangement.losses_at: the residual image tile at bottom-right with the gradient return arrow labelled 'Backpropagate onto NeRF weights'
arrangement.shared: the gradient-filled return arrow joining the two panel colours
